vocabulary.definition: an organism that lives on or in a host organism and gets its food from or at the expense of its host
vocabulary.example: The black hole inside the black hole star was described as a cosmic parasite, consuming matter endlessly.

vocabulary.definition: the science of the origin and development of the universe
vocabulary.example: Studying black hole stars can help solve some of the mysteries in the field of cosmology.

vocabulary.definition: the process of growth or increase, typically by the gradual accumulation of additional layers or matter
vocabulary.example: The accretion disk around the black hole star played a crucial role in its growth and energy release.

vocabulary.definition: a feeling of reverential respect mixed with fear or wonder
vocabulary.example: Witnessing the cosmic beacon created by the black hole star must have been an awe-inspiring experience.

vocabulary.definition: consistently good in quality or performance; able to be trusted
vocabulary.example: Black hole stars could have been reliable seeds for the formation of supermassive black holes in galaxies.

vocabulary.definition: causing or characterized by extreme distress or sorrow
vocabulary.example: The fate of the black hole star, being destroyed by its own black hole, was described as a tragic end.
